subject: Clarify telemetry-derived identifiers & processor boundary for US privacy addendum
messages:
From: Kyle Parker <kyle.parker@acme.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-privacy@acme.com
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify telemetry-derived identifiers & processor boundary for US privacy addendum

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Legal at Acme is running a pass on the US privacy addendum and flagged a couple of items we need clarification on before we sign:

1) Telemetry-derived identifiers: our team wants to confirm whether any device or fingerprint hashes generated by Redwood (e.g., session-derived device hash used for deduping telemetry) would be considered "personal information" under CPRA for purposes of the Service Provider/Processor boundary. If so, can you confirm Redwood's stance on use/reuse and whether these are classified as customer-controlled identifiers?

2) Subprocessor notice: please confirm the cadence and minimum notice (in days) for onboarding new telemetry/logging subprocessors that touch raw logs or crash reports. We need to ensure our incident responders can prepare.

3) Evidence for transit controls: our security team is asking for a simple mapping of where telemetry leaves Redwood's environment (regions, third-party destinations) for redline purposes. A stub CSV would be ideal.

Can you please respond in-thread or share a short mapping? We're aiming to finalize the addendum this week.

Appreciate it,

Kyle Parker
Privacy Counsel — Acme Corp
(kyle.parker@acme.com)

(attachment: acme_questions_0804.pdf / application/pdf)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Parker <kyle.parker@acme.com>
Cc: kart@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify telemetry-derived identifiers & processor boundary for US privacy addendum

Kyle —

Thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Karthik and Soojin for the technical and legal detail. Short answers up front:

1) Telemetry-derived identifiers: by default we treat session/device hashes used strictly for platform operations (dedup, rate-limiting, telemetry aggregation) as within the Service Provider/Processor scope — i.e., processed on behalf of the customer and not repurposed for our own profiling. We can add explicit language in the addendum that "telemetry hashes used for platform operation are treated as Customer Personal Information and will only be used for the delivery and improvement of the Services as directed by Customer."

2) Subprocessor notice: our standard is 30 days' notice for non-emergency additions that process telemetry; for emergency incident responders we can do expedited notification within 72 hours plus retrospective onboarding details. If Acme requires a 45-day notice we can discuss as a commercial concession.

3) Transit mapping: attaching a small CSV that maps telemetry categories (metrics, debug logs, crash dumps), typical retention buckets, and outbound destinations (e.g., S3 in us-west-2 for archived crash dumps; Datadog for metrics). See attached: redwood_telemetry_mapping_v1.csv.

Karthik / Soojin, can you confirm the proposed contractual language for the addendum and whether we should accept a 45-day notice ask?

Thanks,

—Laura Bennett
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
(attachment: redwood_telemetry_mapping_v1.csv / text/csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Kyle Parker <kyle.parker@acme.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify telemetry-derived identifiers & processor boundary for US privacy addendum

Laura / Kyle / Soojin —

Technical note to support contractual wording. We ran a quick inventory:

- Device/session hashes (SHA-256 on session token + salt) are generated transiently and stored only in ephemeral caches used for dedup and KV-cache routing. We do not index or join these hashes against customer PII.
- Crash dumps: may contain PII if customers send full request payloads in logs; by default we recommend customers scrub PII, but if Acme configures full debug retention we can treat crash dumps as Customer Data subject to Customer controls.
- Aggregated metrics (counts, latency histograms): non-identifying by default, retained 90 days for SLOs.

Contract suggestion: add a short definition: "Telemetry-derived identifiers" means hashed/session-derived values generated and used solely for operational purposes and not used for advertising or profiling. Add: "Redwood will not combine telemetry-derived identifiers with external datasets to create user profiles for commercial purposes."

On notice period: 30 days is our standard for planned subprocessors. For telemetry processors (logging/archival/metrics) we can agree to 30 days plus a commitment to notify within 72 hours for emergency incident processors and provide a follow-up impact summary within five business days. That balances operational agility and Acme's review window.

If Acme insists on 45 days we need to flag this to Sales as it may affect our supplier SLAs and onboarding pipeline.

- Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Parker <kyle.parker@acme.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify telemetry-derived identifiers & processor boundary for US privacy addendum

Kyle —

Appreciate the questions; attaching a proposed addendum redline and the DPA addendum PDF we reference internally. Key contractual edits in the redline:

- New definition for "Telemetry-derived identifiers" and explicit prohibition on use for profiling or advertising.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days for planned additions; 72-hour notification for emergency responders + five business day impact summary.
- Transit & retention mapping included as an annex (we referenced the CSV you got).

If that works for you we'll prepare a clean copy and loop your procurement for signature. If Acme needs 45 days please advise and we will escalate for commercial review.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
